top_choice_rationale: P001 rests on one clear physical idea, magic-wavelength trapping, which removes the trade-off between atom number and Doppler/recoil shifts. It was proposed and first demonstrated by Katori and carried to the 1e-18 regime by Ye, and the performance is reproduced and compared across independent laboratories with shifts understood in atomic-structure terms. The two-name allocation is the cleanest on the slate and the citation can name the lattice scheme explicitly, separate from the earlier comb and ion-clock prizes. IceCube (P002) is a genuine first observation in nature and ranks second, but its attribution among three individuals is a judgement call and the origin of the flux remains open. No award ranks last because a mature, well-attributed achievement is available.
recusal_note: No direct tie to Katori or Ye is apparent from the profile; she is a long-time collaborator of 2023 laureate L'Huillier and works in attosecond and atomic-structure theory close to the clock field, a possible but weak AMO-community conflict.
